comment: How the panel presents itself: nothing here is read by the server. The stacking order,
the visibility gate on a confirmation card, which confirmations can be declined, and the
panel's own words for a start that failed, which happens before any server has spoken.
Where the launcher sits, and at what size. A window nobody has moved opens with its
What a confirmation card asks. A write authorises one exact change; leave to work the
page (operate) covers the turn's page operations. Both can be declined. For operate, a
pre-existing draft can also replace the waiting turn, while an empty composer remains locked.
Why the assistant could not start, said in the panel. A start fails before any server
has spoken, so these words cannot be the server's. A sentence is a cause, then what happens
next; the HTTP status stays at the end for whoever has to report it. `final_statuses` are
the failures another attempt cannot fix, so none is made on its own.
